hook: A U.S. Air Force ISR aircrew returning to base from an 11-hour Operation Inherent Resolve surveillance mission over Syria observed a solid, spherical UAP traveling at approximately 424 knots for at least 7 minutes before it passed their aircraft and flew out of range.
why_it_matters: This MISREP is notable because it originates from an operational combat ISR platform — not a training environment — during active counterterrorism surveillance under CENTCOM, lending institutional weight to the observation. The report simultaneously checks 'YES' to advanced capabilities (sustained 424-knot flight by a sphere) while checking 'NO' or 'NONE' to maneuverability, intelligent control, emissions, and equipment effects, illustrating the tension in AARO's standardized reporting taxonomy when applied to anomalous objects. The document's classification level (SECRET//NOFORN, declassification date 2048) and explicit release to AARO confirm it as part of the formal military-to-AARO reporting pipeline established after the UAP disclosure legislation.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was described as solid and spherical ('bouncy ball' shaped), approached from the south at near co-altitude, then dropped altitude and safely passed the aircraft while maintaining approximately 424 knots — a speed sustained consistently for at least 7 minutes.

quotes.text: WHILE RTB AT 2153Z, 1.4a OBSERVED 1X PROB HC UAP SHAPED AS A BOUNCY BALL COME FROM THE SOUTH AT NEAR CO-ALT. 1.4a OBSERVED THE PROB UAP DROP ALTITUDE AND SAFELY PASS THEIR AIRCRAFT WHILE CONSISTANTLY MAINTAINING ~424KN. AFTER 7MIN OF WATCHING, THE PROB UAP BECAME OUT OF RANGE AND 1.4a CARRIED ON THEIR RTB.
UAP Advanced Capabilities And/Or Materials  (yes/no; if yes, describe): YES, TRAVELED ~424KN CONSISTANTLY FOR AT LEAST 7MINS IN THE SHAPE OF A BOUNCY BALL.

key_findings.finding: Despite marking 'YES' to advanced capabilities, the AARO reporting form records no maneuverability observations, no intelligent control, unknown propulsion, and no RF emissions — an internally contradictory data profile.

quotes.text: UAP Under Intelligent Control (yes/no; if yes, describe): NO

key_findings.finding: The observer assessed the UAP as benign, with no emissions detected, no threat to the aircraft or public safety, and no effects on the aircrew or equipment.

quotes.text: NO EMISSIONS CAME FROM THE PROB UAP, UAP WAS NOT CONSIDERED A THREAT TO THE AIRCRAFT OR PUBLIC SAFETY, AND THE UAP HAD NO EFFECTS ON THE AIRCREW.

key_findings.finding: The UAP encounter occurred at the end of a long operational ISR mission — the platform had been on station for 11 hours and 28 minutes conducting target development surveillance of a violent extremist organization before the sighting happened during the return-to-base leg.

quotes.text: Total Time On Station: 11 hours 28 minutes
AT 2153Z, 1.4a OBSERVED AN UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL PHENOMENON AT 37D ST 69 1.4a 07 1.4a (SEE UAP 1).
Global Campaign Plan: GCP - VEO (violent extremist group)

key_findings.finding: The report was formally approved for release to AARO and carries a FVEY releasability caveat, indicating the sighting entered the official allied-shareable UAP reporting pipeline under Operation Inherent Resolve.

quotes.text: Approved for Release to AARO - FOUO/PA

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' on every page and carries the AARO UAP Incident event serial number 092153ZNOV2023-CENTCOM, confirming it was processed through AARO's formal military reporting system.
The Mission Narrative section is classified SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY, indicating the operational ISR data — including the UAP encounter context — was releasable to Five Eyes partners.
